syllabus.title: Basic arithmetic & estimation
syllabus.description: Addition, subtraction, multiplication, division; fractions, decimals, percentages; ratios & proportions; powers, roots, order of operations; scientific notation & estimation; unit conversions (length, area, volume, mass, time, temperature).
syllabus.mastery_goal: Calculate unknowns without advanced university math; quick non-calculator estimation.
syllabus.imatDescription: Identical algebra, proportions, functions, and probabilities tested in IMAT Section 2 and Section 5.

syllabus.title: Algebra, systems & rearranging formulas
syllabus.description: Simple linear equations; two-variable systems; substitution & elimination; rearranging formulas to isolate unknown variables; brackets & signs; constants, variables, coefficients; translating word problems into equations.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Isolate variables rapidly from complex technical formulas without algebra sign errors.
syllabus.imatDescription: Identical algebra, proportions, functions, and probabilities tested in IMAT Section 2 and Section 5.

syllabus.title: Ratios, rates & proportionality
syllabus.description: Direct and inverse proportionality; ratios between gear rotations or dimensions; speed, distance, time; work rate, flow rate, production rate; percentage increase and decrease; scale factors & geometric enlargement.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Apply direct/inverse proportionality to physical flow rates, work rates, and scaling.
syllabus.imatDescription: Identical algebra, proportions, functions, and probabilities tested in IMAT Section 2 and Section 5.

syllabus.title: Geometry, scaling & dimensions
syllabus.description: Perimeter & area (triangles, rectangles, circles); circumference & circle area; surface area & volume (cubes, cuboids, cylinders, spheres); angles & basic trigonometry; length/area/volume scaling; calculating dimensions from technical diagrams.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Compute volumes, surface areas, and 2D/3D scaling factors from geometric drawings.
syllabus.imatDescription: Identical algebra, proportions, functions, and probabilities tested in IMAT Section 2 and Section 5.

syllabus.title: Functions, rates & linearity
syllabus.description: Linear relationships; increasing and decreasing functions; constant versus changing rates; reading values from a function; comparing two or more mathematical expressions; recognising linear vs nonlinear trends.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Determine whether physical relationships are linear, quadratic, or inversely asymptotic.
syllabus.imatDescription: Identical algebra, proportions, functions, and probabilities tested in IMAT Section 2 and Section 5.

syllabus.title: Statistics, datasets & trends
syllabus.description: Mean, median, range; reading numerical tables; comparing datasets; percentages and ratios in data; basic probability & uncertainty; identifying trends and outliers in simple datasets.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Extract statistical conclusions, medians, and anomaly points from complex numerical tables.
syllabus.imatDescription: Identical algebra, proportions, functions, and probabilities tested in IMAT Section 2 and Section 5.

syllabus.title: Physical quantities, SI units & vectors
syllabus.description: SI units and derived units; mass, weight, length, time, temperature; scalar and vector quantities; unit conversions; physical symbols in formulas.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Dimensional analysis and rapid conversion across metric prefixes and derived units.
syllabus.imatDescription: Core kinematics, Newton's laws, energy conservation, and hydrostatic pressure tested in IMAT Section 5.

syllabus.title: Kinematics & motion graphs
syllabus.description: Distance and displacement; speed and velocity; acceleration and deceleration; uniform & non-uniform motion; distance-time & speed-time graphs; effects of braking and acceleration.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Interpret velocity-time gradients and area under curve to deduce displacement and braking.
syllabus.imatDescription: Core kinematics, Newton's laws, energy conservation, and hydrostatic pressure tested in IMAT Section 5.

syllabus.title: Forces, Newton's laws & friction
syllabus.description: Force & resultant force; Newton's laws at a basic level; gravity and weight; friction; normal force & support forces; opposite forces; how forces affect movement.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Resolve opposing forces, friction coefficients, and resultant accelerations on bodies.
syllabus.imatDescription: Core kinematics, Newton's laws, energy conservation, and hydrostatic pressure tested in IMAT Section 5.

syllabus.title: Work, energy conservation & power
syllabus.description: Work done by a force (W = Fd); kinetic and potential energy; energy transformation & conservation; power as rate of energy transfer; efficiency & energy losses; force-distance-time-energy relationships.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Calculate mechanical work, energy losses, and system efficiency percentages.
syllabus.imatDescription: Core kinematics, Newton's laws, energy conservation, and hydrostatic pressure tested in IMAT Section 5.

syllabus.title: Fluids, pressure & buoyancy
syllabus.description: Pressure and force per unit area (P = F/A); density; buoyancy, floating & sinking; displaced volume (Archimedes principle); qualitative fluid-flow; pipe dimensions and flow rates.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Master official digital buoyancy testlets: predict floating height and displaced fluid mass.
syllabus.imatDescription: Core kinematics, Newton's laws, energy conservation, and hydrostatic pressure tested in IMAT Section 5.

syllabus.title: Heat, thermal expansion & gas states
syllabus.description: Difference between heat and temperature; thermal expansion; heat transfer; temperature changes; pressure and volume changes in gases; energy transfer between systems.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Understand qualitative thermodynamic shifts in enclosed volumes and thermal equilibrium.
syllabus.imatDescription: Core kinematics, Newton's laws, energy conservation, and hydrostatic pressure tested in IMAT Section 5.

syllabus.title: Gears, gear ratios & rotation speed
syllabus.description: Gear mechanisms & gear ratios; number of teeth vs rotational speed (N1ω1 = N2ω2); rotations of connected gears; direction of rotation (clockwise/counter-clockwise); comparing large vs small gears; motion transmission in mechanisms.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Predict exact rotation direction and revolutions per minute through interconnected gear trains.
syllabus.imatDescription: Moments of force, torque, mechanical advantage, levers, and Hooke's law springs tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Levers, pulleys & mechanical advantage
syllabus.description: Fulcrums & lever arms; input force vs output force; load and effort; simple pulley systems; rope and wheel arrangements; how change in force or distance affects mechanism.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Compute mechanical advantage and required pulling force in multiple-pulley tackle systems.
syllabus.imatDescription: Moments of force, torque, mechanical advantage, levers, and Hooke's law springs tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Torque & balanced moments
syllabus.description: Meaning of torque (τ = Fd); force acting at distance from pivot; balanced & unbalanced moments; comparing forces at different distances from fulcrum; predicting which side moves downward.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Equate clockwise and counter-clockwise moments to determine pivot equilibrium or tilt.
syllabus.imatDescription: Moments of force, torque, mechanical advantage, levers, and Hooke's law springs tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Beams, supports & equilibrium
syllabus.description: Pivots, bearings & supports; loads acting on beam; tension & compression basic; conditions for mechanical balance; moving supports or loads; connected beams, ropes and hooks.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Analyze support reaction forces when point loads shift along a static beam.
syllabus.imatDescription: Moments of force, torque, mechanical advantage, levers, and Hooke's law springs tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Springs, elasticity & deformation
syllabus.description: Compression & extension; elastic vs permanent deformation; stiffness (k) & flexibility; effect of dimensions on stiffness; applied force vs deformation relationships (Hooke's law).
syllabus.mastery_goal: Calculate parallel and series spring constants and extension under variable weights.
syllabus.imatDescription: Moments of force, torque, mechanical advantage, levers, and Hooke's law springs tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Kinematic linkage & transmission
syllabus.description: Input and output motion; direction and magnitude of movement; speed transmission; simple machine mechanisms; cause-and-effect relationships between connected components.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Trace motion propagation through crankshafts, cams, pistons, and sliding linkages.
syllabus.imatDescription: Moments of force, torque, mechanical advantage, levers, and Hooke's law springs tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.chapter: 4. Formulas, Graphs, Tables and Technical Relationships
syllabus.title: Translating verbal descriptions into formulas
syllabus.description: Turning verbal descriptions into equations; identifying known vs unknown variables; recognizing dependent variables; rearranging supplied formulas; substituting values; comparing systems equations.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Directly convert technical scenario descriptions into exact symbolic mathematical formulas.
syllabus.imatBadge: IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving & Graph Interpretation
syllabus.imatDescription: Direct/inverse proportions, multi-source tabular data, and formula translation tested in IMAT Section 2.

syllabus.chapter: 4. Formulas, Graphs, Tables and Technical Relationships
syllabus.title: Direct, inverse & compound relationships
syllabus.description: When one increases, another increases/decreases; constant relationships; linear and nonlinear relationships; products, ratios and differences; determining permissible system changes.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Identify qualitative dependencies (e.g. doubling pipe radius quadruples cross-sectional area).
syllabus.imatBadge: IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving & Graph Interpretation
syllabus.imatDescription: Direct/inverse proportions, multi-source tabular data, and formula translation tested in IMAT Section 2.

syllabus.chapter: 4. Formulas, Graphs, Tables and Technical Relationships
syllabus.title: Graph interpretation & qualitative matching
syllabus.description: Reading horizontal/vertical axes; scales & units; coordinates & values; increasing, decreasing, constant sections; slopes & inflection points; selecting correct qualitative graph for a relationship.
syllabus.mastery_goal: From 4 candidate graphs, identify the precise curve matching a described technical law.
syllabus.imatBadge: IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving & Graph Interpretation
syllabus.imatDescription: Direct/inverse proportions, multi-source tabular data, and formula translation tested in IMAT Section 2.

syllabus.chapter: 4. Formulas, Graphs, Tables and Technical Relationships
syllabus.title: Technical tables & multi-source data
syllabus.description: Extracting information from tables; comparing rows and columns; calculating differences and ratios; identifying max and min values; combining data from multiple sources; verifying valid conclusions.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Filter and synthesize multi-variable matrices without getting misled by distractors.
syllabus.imatBadge: IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving & Graph Interpretation
syllabus.imatDescription: Direct/inverse proportions, multi-source tabular data, and formula translation tested in IMAT Section 2.

syllabus.chapter: 4. Formulas, Graphs, Tables and Technical Relationships
syllabus.title: Technical illustrations & component tracking
syllabus.description: Interpreting component labels; following relationships in diagrams; comparing mechanical arrangements; identifying input, output, intermediate stages; effect of changing one component.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Follow system schematics to predict failure modes or downstream performance drops.
syllabus.imatBadge: IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving & Graph Interpretation
syllabus.imatDescription: Direct/inverse proportions, multi-source tabular data, and formula translation tested in IMAT Section 2.

syllabus.chapter: 4. Formulas, Graphs, Tables and Technical Relationships
syllabus.title: Flow & process diagrams
syllabus.description: Tracing path from input to output; tracking quantities through pipes/components; branches and merging flows; checking conservation laws under given conditions; comparing configurations.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Calculate mass/fluid flow conservation across converging and diverging junctions.
syllabus.imatBadge: IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving & Graph Interpretation
syllabus.imatDescription: Direct/inverse proportions, multi-source tabular data, and formula translation tested in IMAT Section 2.

syllabus.title: 3D mental rotation & viewing angles
syllabus.description: Mentally rotating a solid; viewing from front, rear, left, right, above, below; identifying rotated version; distinguishing rotation from reflection; tracking visible surfaces.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Rapidly recognize 3D rotated solids without physical models under strict timed limits.
syllabus.imatDescription: 3D orthographic and axonometric projection skills (supplementary cognitive training).

syllabus.title: Orthographic projections & missing views
syllabus.description: Front, side, and top views; matching views of same solid; predicting missing third view from two supplied views; parallel projection; recognizing orientation from drawing.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Deduce the missing side or top view given front and plan elevation drawings.
syllabus.imatDescription: 3D orthographic and axonometric projection skills (supplementary cognitive training).

syllabus.title: Composite solids, cut-outs & stepped blocks
syllabus.description: Cube and cuboid arrangements; objects with cut-outs; stepped and irregular solids; missing sections; hidden surfaces and edges; component interlock.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Count cubes and identify hidden contact faces in complex 3D block assemblies.
syllabus.imatDescription: 3D orthographic and axonometric projection skills (supplementary cognitive training).

syllabus.title: Spatial tracking of cables & rods
syllabus.description: Tracking lines, rods, ropes, cables inside transparent enclosure; front vs behind passing; viewpoint matching; endpoints and direction tracking.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Trace intertwined cables through 3D cubic frames and identify start/end coordinates.
syllabus.imatDescription: 3D orthographic and axonometric projection skills (supplementary cognitive training).

syllabus.title: Reflection, symmetry & chirality
syllabus.description: Mirror images; rotational symmetry; corresponding surfaces and edges; understanding orientation changes after combined rotation and reflection.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Distinguish between chiral mirror enantiomorphs and legitimate physical rotations.
syllabus.imatDescription: 3D orthographic and axonometric projection skills (supplementary cognitive training).

syllabus.title: Voltage, current, resistance & power
syllabus.description: Voltage (V), current (I), resistance (R); electrical power (P); energy consumption; units of electrical quantities (Volts, Amperes, Ohms, Watts); relationships between electrical variables.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Relate V, I, R, and Power consumption across electrical components.
syllabus.imatBadge: IMAT Overlap: Physics (DC Circuits & Ohm's Law)
syllabus.imatDescription: Resistors in series/parallel, Ohm's law, electrical power dissipation, and Kirchhoff's rules tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Circuit diagrams & schematic symbols
syllabus.description: Cells, batteries, wires, resistors; switches and circuit connections; open and closed circuits; identifying components from standard symbols; following current paths in simple circuits.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Identify open circuits, active loops, and electrical node connections.
syllabus.imatBadge: IMAT Overlap: Physics (DC Circuits & Ohm's Law)
syllabus.imatDescription: Resistors in series/parallel, Ohm's law, electrical power dissipation, and Kirchhoff's rules tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Series & parallel circuits & equivalent R
syllabus.description: Components in series; components in parallel; equivalent resistance (Req); alternative current paths; predicting consequences of component removal or branch disconnection.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Calculate equivalent resistance and branch currents in mixed bridge circuits.
syllabus.imatBadge: IMAT Overlap: Physics (DC Circuits & Ohm's Law)
syllabus.imatDescription: Resistors in series/parallel, Ohm's law, electrical power dissipation, and Kirchhoff's rules tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Ohm's law & power dissipation
syllabus.description: Ohm's law (V = IR); current and voltage under different loads; effect of changing resistor values; basic power calculations (P = I²R); consistent vs inconsistent circuit arrangements.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Determine how voltage drops divide across unequal resistors in a closed circuit.
syllabus.imatBadge: IMAT Overlap: Physics (DC Circuits & Ohm's Law)
syllabus.imatDescription: Resistors in series/parallel, Ohm's law, electrical power dissipation, and Kirchhoff's rules tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Technical schematics & short-circuit detection
syllabus.description: Tracing connected components; identifying short circuits or disconnected paths in schematics; comparing internal circuit arrangements; inferring electrical properties from measurements.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Spot accidental zero-resistance short circuits bypassing loads in complex wiring diagrams.
syllabus.imatBadge: IMAT Overlap: Physics (DC Circuits & Ohm's Law)
syllabus.imatDescription: Resistors in series/parallel, Ohm's law, electrical power dissipation, and Kirchhoff's rules tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Technical drawing fundamentals & section views
syllabus.description: Reading dimensions and labels; understanding scale; distinguishing visible and hidden edges; interpreting simple section drawings; recognizing basic drafting conventions.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Read cross-sectional hatching and dashed lines to understand internal part cavities.
syllabus.imatDescription: Component assemblies and exploded drawings (German engineering specific).

syllabus.title: Component assembly & exploded views
syllabus.description: Identifying how components connect; matching assembled objects to individual component drawings; understanding order of assembly steps; identifying incompatible arrangements.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Determine proper mating sequences and detect interference in component fits.
syllabus.imatDescription: Component assemblies and exploded drawings (German engineering specific).

syllabus.title: Geometric construction & part alterations
syllabus.description: Matching 3D components to drawings; recognizing how cuts, holes, or protrusions change shapes; comparing design alternatives; understanding basic dimensional constraints.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Evaluate geometric tolerances and how machining cuts alter original raw profiles.
syllabus.imatDescription: Component assemblies and exploded drawings (German engineering specific).

syllabus.title: Design constraints & feasibility selection
syllabus.description: Identifying which proposed design satisfies given conditions; comparing alternative configurations; recognizing properties that stay constant after change; selecting feasible solutions.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Pick the single engineering design variant that satisfies all stated functional constraints.
syllabus.imatDescription: Component assemblies and exploded drawings (German engineering specific).

syllabus.title: Physical & mechanical material properties
syllabus.description: Density; hardness; strength; stiffness; elasticity and plastic deformation; thermal and electrical conductivity; resistance to heat or corrosion.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Differentiate between tensile strength, yield stress, hardness, and Young's modulus.
syllabus.imatDescription: Stress-strain curves, Young's modulus, and thermal expansion tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Metals, alloys & operational loads
syllabus.description: Basic properties of metals and alloys; comparing material performance; why different applications require specific materials; effects of mechanical loads and temperature.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Compare aluminum, steel, and titanium for strength-to-weight and thermal applications.
syllabus.imatDescription: Stress-strain curves, Young's modulus, and thermal expansion tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Polymers: Thermoplastics, thermosets & elastomers
syllabus.description: Thermoplastics (meltable/recyclable); thermosets (cross-linked, heat-resistant); elastomers (high reversible elasticity); behavior under heating, cooling, and applied force.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Official digital testlet focus: predict plastic deformation under elevated temperatures.
syllabus.imatDescription: Stress-strain curves, Young's modulus, and thermal expansion tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Material selection from specifications
syllabus.description: Selecting suitable materials for specified use; comparing strength, flexibility, heat resistance; identifying relevant properties from descriptions; matching properties to applications.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Match multi-criteria engineering requirements to the best material candidate table.
syllabus.imatDescription: Stress-strain curves, Young's modulus, and thermal expansion tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Thermal equilibrium & expansion
syllabus.description: Difference between heat (energy) and temperature (kinetic measure); thermal expansion; heating and cooling curves; reaching thermal equilibrium.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Distinguish latent heat from sensible heat and compute basic linear expansion.
syllabus.imatDescription: Ideal gas laws (PV=nRT), thermodynamic P-V state cycles, Carnot efficiency, and heat transfer tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Heat transfer, conservation & efficiency
syllabus.description: Heat transfer mechanisms (conduction, convection, radiation); energy conservation; energy input vs useful output; thermal losses and thermodynamic efficiency.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Calculate Carnot and mechanical thermal efficiency ratios in heat engine scenarios.
syllabus.imatDescription: Ideal gas laws (PV=nRT), thermodynamic P-V state cycles, Carnot efficiency, and heat transfer tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Gas laws & rigid container states
syllabus.description: Qualitative relationships between pressure, volume, temperature (PV = nRT); gas behavior in rigid containers; interpreting supplied physical gas laws; cause-and-effect.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Predict pressure increases when sealed rigid gas vessels undergo heating.
syllabus.imatDescription: Ideal gas laws (PV=nRT), thermodynamic P-V state cycles, Carnot efficiency, and heat transfer tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: P-V & T-S state diagrams
syllabus.description: Reading pressure or temperature changes on graphs; following systems through state cycles; comparing possible thermodynamic system behaviors; interpreting formulas.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Trace isobaric, isochoric, and isothermal paths on indicator diagrams.
syllabus.imatDescription: Ideal gas laws (PV=nRT), thermodynamic P-V state cycles, Carnot efficiency, and heat transfer tested in IMAT Physics.

syllabus.title: Atoms, molecules & physical/chemical changes
syllabus.description: Elements and compounds; atoms and molecules; mixtures vs pure substances; simple chemical formulas; basic physical and chemical changes.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Comprehend chemical composition labels and physical state changes.
syllabus.imatDescription: Atomic structures, solution molarity, gas laws, and reaction stoichiometry tested in IMAT Section 4.

syllabus.title: Metals, corrosion & chemical resistance
syllabus.description: Metals and non-metals; basic corrosion concepts (oxidation, galvanic corrosion); chemical resistance of materials; composition vs material properties.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Recognize oxidation and galvanic corrosion mechanisms in moist environments.
syllabus.imatDescription: Atomic structures, solution molarity, gas laws, and reaction stoichiometry tested in IMAT Section 4.

syllabus.title: Monomers, polymers & synthesis
syllabus.description: Monomers and polymers; basic polymerisation concepts; comparing different classes of plastics using supplied chemical information.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Read supplied chemical descriptions of synthetic polymers to assess application suitability.
syllabus.imatDescription: Atomic structures, solution molarity, gas laws, and reaction stoichiometry tested in IMAT Section 4.

syllabus.title: Chemical data interpretation & tables
syllabus.description: Understanding supplied substance descriptions; reading simple chemical diagrams & tables; matching stated chemical properties to practical engineering use.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Extract chemical safety, reactivity, and phase behavior from technical data sheets.
syllabus.imatDescription: Atomic structures, solution molarity, gas laws, and reaction stoichiometry tested in IMAT Section 4.

syllabus.title: Boolean logic & truth evaluations
syllabus.description: Basic Boolean logic; AND, OR, and NOT operators; evaluating logical conditions; recognizing valid and invalid truth combinations.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Evaluate compound Boolean conditions in logic gates and conditional decisions.
syllabus.imatDescription: Boolean logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, XOR) and decision flowcharts tested in IMAT Section 2.

syllabus.title: Algorithms, flowcharts & decision branches
syllabus.description: Understanding sequences of instructions; following processes or flowcharts; recognizing conditions and alternative paths; identifying procedure output.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Trace algorithm flowcharts step-by-step and determine terminal variable values.
syllabus.imatDescription: Boolean logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, XOR) and decision flowcharts tested in IMAT Section 2.

syllabus.title: Input, processing, loops & pseudocode
syllabus.description: Input, processing, output; tracking changes to variables; interpreting simple pseudocode; applying stated rules to unfamiliar computational processes.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Step through loop iterations and conditional mutations without syntax confusion.
syllabus.imatDescription: Boolean logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, XOR) and decision flowcharts tested in IMAT Section 2.

syllabus.title: Position, grid edges & boundary bounces
syllabus.description: Horizontal, vertical, diagonal movement; clockwise and anticlockwise movement; movement along edges of a grid; movement that reverses at boundary.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Track geometric symbol movements across discrete grid positions under 1 min/item.
syllabus.imatDescription: Sequential pattern transformations.

syllabus.title: Rotation (90°, 180°, 270°) & repeated cycles
syllabus.description: Rotation by 90°, 180°, 270°; changes in orientation of symbols; detecting repeated rotation patterns; combining rotation with translational movement.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Disentangle rotation rules from spatial shifts across successive frames.
syllabus.imatDescription: Sequential pattern transformations.

syllabus.title: Colour alternation & shape mutations
syllabus.description: Alternating colors; repeating color sequences; changes in shape or orientation; multiple rules operating simultaneously.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Isolate color periodicity and shape progression as independent variables.
syllabus.imatDescription: Sequential pattern transformations.

syllabus.title: Compound multi-figure patterns
syllabus.description: Two or more changing figures; different rules in different rows or columns; increasing movement steps; recognizing next pattern when rule is not obvious.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Solve 20 items in 25 minutes by decomposing compound visual rules.
syllabus.imatDescription: Sequential pattern transformations.

syllabus.title: Arithmetic operations & small integers
syllabus.description: Addition, subtraction, multiplication, division; inverse operations; working efficiently with small positive integers (1 to 20).
syllabus.mastery_goal: Fast mental arithmetic without written calculations under 75 seconds per system.
syllabus.imatDescription: Simultaneous linear equations and arithmetic constraint satisfaction tested in IMAT Section 2 & 5.

syllabus.title: Multi-variable symbolic systems
syllabus.description: Solving two or more equations together; substitution; elimination; identifying relationships between unknowns; checking that every equation is satisfied.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Spot equations with only one unknown or difference relationships to unlock systems.
syllabus.imatDescription: Simultaneous linear equations and arithmetic constraint satisfaction tested in IMAT Section 2 & 5.

syllabus.title: Integer constraints (1 to 20)
syllabus.description: Finding values for several letters; understanding that every equation in system must be correct; working with stated integer constraints (1–20); simplifying equations.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Apply divisibility rules and upper bound constraints to deduce letter values.
syllabus.imatDescription: Simultaneous linear equations and arithmetic constraint satisfaction tested in IMAT Section 2 & 5.

syllabus.title: Speed, elimination & error checking
syllabus.description: Solving equations without lengthy written working; using known values to eliminate possibilities; checking for arithmetic errors. (Target: 20 systems in 25 min).
syllabus.mastery_goal: Complete all 20 systems in under 25 minutes with zero algebraic sign blunders.
syllabus.imatDescription: Simultaneous linear equations and arithmetic constraint satisfaction tested in IMAT Section 2 & 5.

syllabus.title: 5 × 5 grid rules (Letters A, B, C, D, E)
syllabus.description: Working with a 5 × 5 grid; understanding rows and columns; using letters A, B, C, D and E; ensuring each letter appears only once in every row and column.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Internalize strict Latin square uniqueness constraints across 5 rows and 5 columns.
syllabus.imatDescription: Combinatorial Latin squares and candidate grid elimination.

syllabus.title: Candidate elimination & mental cell filling
syllabus.description: Identifying missing letters; eliminating impossible values; combining row and column restrictions; filling one cell mentally to determine another; unique satisfying values.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Cross-reference row and column intersections mentally without scratchpad marks.
syllabus.imatDescription: Combinatorial Latin squares and candidate grid elimination.

syllabus.title: Fast strategies & high-density start points
syllabus.description: Start with row or column containing the most information (3–4 knowns); eliminate candidates before testing; check row & column conditions; avoid over-investing time on single grid.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Solve 20 Latin Squares within 25 minutes by targeting maximum-density vectors.
syllabus.imatDescription: Combinatorial Latin squares and candidate grid elimination.

syllabus.title: Quantitative Problems (22 Qs / 45 min)
syllabus.description: Arithmetic word problems; percentages, ratios & proportions; averages and age problems; rates, quantities, unit conversions; multi-step calculations; paragraph interpretation.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Extract numbers from text paragraphs and execute multi-step calculations in ~2 min/item.
syllabus.imatDescription: General quantitative reasoning, verbal analogies, and numerical series.

syllabus.title: Inferring Relationships (22 Qs / 10 min - Strict Speed)
syllabus.description: Word analogies; matching words with equivalent logical relationships; categories and associations; inferring rules from examples. (Extremely strict: 27 seconds per question!).
syllabus.mastery_goal: Rapid semantic pairing and association matching at 27 seconds per question.
syllabus.imatDescription: General quantitative reasoning, verbal analogies, and numerical series.

syllabus.title: Completing Patterns (22 Qs / 20 min)
syllabus.description: Visual sequences; missing geometric figures; rotations and reflections; symmetry; changes in shape, number or position; identifying the next figure from a visual rule.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Matrix pattern completion across 3x3 geometric grids.
syllabus.imatDescription: General quantitative reasoning, verbal analogies, and numerical series.

syllabus.title: Continuing Numerical Series (22 Qs / 25 min)
syllabus.description: Addition and subtraction sequences; multiplication and division patterns; alternating rules; differences between successive numbers; increasing/decreasing differences; compound sequences.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Detect two-tier and alternating operational sequences under 65 seconds per series.
syllabus.imatDescription: General quantitative reasoning, verbal analogies, and numerical series.

syllabus.title: Formalising Technical Interrelationships (22 Qs / 31.4% Qs / 60 min)
syllabus.description: Translate descriptions into formulas, rearrange equations, compare gears and identify how technical variables are mathematically related.
syllabus.mastery_goal: Symbolic formula translation and equation manipulation under exam time.

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: Two pipes are used to fill an empty water reservoir. Working alone, Pipe A can fill the reservoir in 6 hours, while Pipe B can fill it in 12 hours. If both pipes are opened simultaneously at full flow, how many hours will it take to fill the reservoir completely?
questions.question_de: Zwei Rohre dienen dem Befüllen eines leeren Wasserbehälters. Rohr A allein benötigt 6 Stunden, Rohr B allein 12 Stunden. Wie viele Stunden dauert die vollständige Befüllung, wenn beide Rohre gleichzeitig mit voller Leistung geöffnet werden?
questions.explanation: Work rate formula for simultaneous tasks: 1/t_total = 1/t_A + 1/t_B. Here, 1/6 + 1/12 = 2/12 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 reservoir per hour. Inverting gives t_total = 4 hours. Option A is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Formel für gleichzeitige Arbeitsraten: 1/t_ges = 1/t_A + 1/t_B. Hier: 1/6 + 1/12 = 2/12 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 Behälter pro Stunde. Kehrwert: t_ges = 4 Stunden. Option A ist richtig.
questions.trap: Taking the arithmetic average of the two filling times: (6 + 12) / 2 = 9 hours (Option D), or subtracting 12 - 6 = 6 hours (Option C).
questions.trap_de: Arithmetisches Mittel der Zeiten berechnet: (6 + 12) / 2 = 9 Stunden (Option D), oder 12 - 6 = 6 Stunden (Option C).
questions.fast_track: Product over sum shortcut: t = (6 × 12) / (6 + 12) = 72 / 18 = 4 hours.
questions.fast_track_de: Produkt durch Summe: (6  12) / (6 + 12) = 72 / 18 = 4 Stunden.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving: Work-Rate & Fluid Systems

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: Three printing presses (P1, P2, and P3) are used to print an edition of an exam booklet. Operating independently, P1 requires 3 hours, P2 requires 6 hours, and P3 requires 2 hours to complete the entire run. If all three presses run simultaneously without interruption, how many minutes will the job take?
questions.question_de: Drei Druckmaschinen (P1, P2 und P3) drucken eine Auflage von Prüfungsheften. P1 allein benötigt 3 Stunden, P2 benötigt 6 Stunden und P3 benötigt 2 Stunden. Wie viele Minuten dauert der Druckvorgang, wenn alle drei Maschinen gleichzeitig arbeiten?
questions.explanation: Add the hourly production rates: Rate = 1/3 + 1/6 + 1/2 = 2/6 + 1/6 + 3/6 = 6/6 = 1 complete run per hour. Thus, the total time required is exactly 1 hour = 60 minutes. Option B is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Summe der stündlichen Produktionsraten: 1/3 + 1/6 + 1/2 = 2/6 + 1/6 + 3/6 = 6/6 = 1 Auftrag pro Stunde. Die benötigte Zeit beträgt exakt 1 Stunde = 60 Minuten. Option B ist richtig.
questions.trap: Averaging the times (3 + 6 + 2)/3 = 3.67 hours = 220 min, or confusing 1 hour with 100 minutes.
questions.trap_de: Zeiten arithmetisch gemittelt (3 + 6 + 2)/3 = 3,67 Stunden, statt Kehrwerte zu addieren.
questions.fast_track: Common denominator 6: rates are 2/6 + 1/6 + 3/6 = 6/6 = 1 job/hour -> 60 minutes.
questions.fast_track_de: Hauptnenner 6: Raten ergeben 2 + 1 + 3 = 6 Sechstel -> 1 Auftrag/Stunde = 60 Minuten.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Mathematics & Problem Solving: Algebraic Systems

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: An inlet valve can fill a storage tank in 8 hours. A drain valve located at the bottom can empty the completely full tank in 12 hours. If the tank is initially empty and both valves are opened at the same time, how many hours will it take for the tank to be filled completely?
questions.question_de: Ein Einlassventil kann einen Vorratstank in 8 Stunden füllen. Ein Bodenablassventil kann den vollen Tank in 12 Stunden vollständig entleeren. Wie viele Stunden dauert es, bis der anfangs leere Tank vollständig gefüllt ist, wenn beide Ventile gleichzeitig geöffnet werden?
questions.explanation: Net filling rate = Rate_in - Rate_out = 1/8 - 1/12. Using common denominator 24: 3/24 - 2/24 = 1/24 of the tank per hour. Time to fill completely = 1 / (1/24) = 24 hours. Option C is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Netto-Füllrate = Zulauf - Ablauf = 1/8 - 1/12 = 3/24 - 2/24 = 1/24 des Tanks pro Stunde. Fülldauer = Kehrwert von 1/24 = 24 Stunden. Option C ist richtig.
questions.trap: Adding the rates instead of subtracting: 1/8 + 1/12 = 5/24 -> 4.8 hours, or simply subtracting times 12 - 8 = 4 hours.
questions.trap_de: Raten addiert statt subtrahiert (1/8 + 1/12) oder schlicht die Differenz der Zeiten (12 - 8 = 4 h) gebildet.
questions.fast_track_de: Nettorate = 3/24 - 2/24 = 1/24 -> 24 Stunden.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving: Work-Rate & Fluid Systems

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: Two technicians, Lukas and Mia, can assemble an industrial prototype together in 10 hours. Lukas working alone would require 15 hours to complete the assembly. How many hours would Mia require to assemble the prototype entirely on her own?
questions.question_de: Zwei Techniker, Lukas und Mia, können einen Industrie-Prototyp gemeinsam in 10 Stunden montieren. Lukas allein würde dafür 15 Stunden benötigen. Wie viele Stunden würde Mia benötigen, um den Prototyp völlig allein zu montieren?
questions.explanation: Combined rate: 1/t_tot = 1/t_Lukas + 1/t_Mia. Thus 1/10 = 1/15 + 1/t_Mia -> 1/t_Mia = 1/10 - 1/15 = 3/30 - 2/30 = 1/30. Mia alone takes 30 hours. Option D is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Kombinierte Rate: 1/10 = 1/15 + 1/t_Mia. Umformen: 1/t_Mia = 1/10 - 1/15 = 3/30 - 2/30 = 1/30. Mia allein benötigt also 30 Stunden. Option D ist richtig.
questions.trap: Subtracting times directly: 15 - 10 = 5 hours, or assuming Mia must take 20 or 25 hours.
questions.trap_de: Einfache Subtraktion der Zeiten (15 - 10 = 5 h) statt Subtraktion der Kehrwerte.
questions.fast_track_de: Differenz-Formel: (10  15) / (15 - 10) = 150 / 5 = 30 Stunden.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Mathematics & Problem Solving: Algebraic Systems

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: Machine Alpha can manufacture a production batch in 12 hours, while Machine Beta can produce the same batch in 18 hours. Machine Alpha begins running alone and operates for 4 hours. At that point, Machine Beta is switched on, and both machines work together until the batch is finished. How many additional hours do the two machines work together?
questions.question_de: Maschine Alpha kann eine Produktionscharge in 12 Stunden fertigen, Maschine Beta in 18 Stunden. Maschine Alpha läuft zunächst 4 Stunden allein. Danach wird Maschine Beta zugeschaltet, und beide arbeiten gemeinsam bis zur Fertigstellung. Wie viele zusätzliche Stunden arbeiten beide Maschinen gemeinsam?
questions.explanation: In 4 hours, Machine Alpha completes 4/12 = 1/3 of the batch. The remaining fraction is 1 - 1/3 = 2/3. Combined rate of Alpha and Beta = 1/12 + 1/18 = 3/36 + 2/36 = 5/36 batch/hour. Additional time together = (2/3) / (5/36) = (24/36) / (5/36) = 24/5 = 4.8 hours (4 hours 48 minutes). Option A is correct.
questions.explanation_de: In 4 Stunden fertigt Maschine Alpha 4/12 = 1/3 der Charge. Verbleibender Anteil: 2/3. Gemeinsame Rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 pro Stunde. Benötigte gemeinsame Restzeit = (2/3) / (5/36) = 24/5 = 4,8 Stunden. Option A ist richtig.
questions.trap: Adding Alpha's initial 4 hours to the answer (4 + 4.8 = 8.8 h), or assuming half of the job was completed in the first 4 hours.
questions.trap_de: Die anfänglichen 4 Stunden zur Restzeit addiert (8,8 h) statt nur nach der gemeinsamen Restzeit zu fragen.
questions.fast_track: Remaining fraction: 2/3. Combined rate: 5/36. Time = (2/3) × (36/5) = 24/5 = 4.8 hours.
questions.fast_track_de: Restanteil: 2/3. Gemeinsame Rate: 5/36. Zeit = 24/5 = 4,8 Stunden.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Mathematics & Problem Solving: Algebraic Systems

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: Three specialized lab assistants (A, B, and C) process clinical samples. Working in pairs, A and B can complete a test series in 6 hours; B and C can complete it in 8 hours; and A and C can complete it in 12 hours. If all three work together simultaneously, how long will they take to complete the test series?
questions.question_de: Drei Laborassistenten (A, B und C) werten Testreihen aus. Im Zweierteam benötigen A und B zusammen 6 Stunden, B und C 8 Stunden und A und C 12 Stunden. Wie lange benötigen alle drei Assistenten gemeinsam, wenn sie gleichzeitig arbeiten?
questions.explanation: Add the pairwise rates: (A + B) + (B + C) + (A + C) = 2(A + B + C) = 1/6 + 1/8 + 1/12. Using common denominator 24: 4/24 + 3/24 + 2/24 = 9/24 = 3/8. Therefore, A + B + C = (3/8) / 2 = 3/16 job per hour. Total time = 16/3 hours = 5 1/3 hours = 5 hours 20 minutes. Option B is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Addition der paarweisen Raten: 2(A + B + C) = 1/6 + 1/8 + 1/12 = 4/24 + 3/24 + 2/24 = 9/24 = 3/8. Folglich ist A + B + C = 3/16 pro Stunde. Zeit = 16/3 Stunden = 5 Stunden und 20 Minuten. Option B ist richtig.
questions.trap: Forgetting to divide by 2 after adding the equations, yielding 24/9 = 8/3 = 2 h 40 min.
questions.trap_de: Vergessen, durch 2 zu teilen (da jeder Assistent doppelt gezählt wurde), was zu 2 h 40 min führt.
questions.fast_track: Sum of rates = 9/24 = 3/8. Combined rate = 3/16. Time = 16/3 h = 5 h 20 min.
questions.fast_track_de: Summe = 9/24. Dreier-Rate = 9/48 = 3/16 -> Kehrwert 16/3 h = 5 h 20 min.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Mathematics & Problem Solving: Algebraic Systems

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: A water reservoir can normally be filled completely by a supply pump in 5 hours. However, due to an undiscovered leak at the bottom of the reservoir, it takes 6 hours to fill the reservoir completely. If the supply pump is turned off when the reservoir is completely full, how many hours will it take for the leak to empty the entire reservoir?
questions.question_de: Ein Wasserspeicher kann von einer Pumpe normalerweise in 5 Stunden vollständig gefüllt werden. Wegen eines Lecks am Boden dauert die Befüllung jedoch 6 Stunden. Wenn die Pumpe bei vollem Speicher abgeschaltet wird: Wie viele Stunden dauert es, bis das Leck den Speicher komplett entleert hat?
questions.explanation: Rate of pump = 1/5 reservoir/h. Net rate with leak = 1/6 reservoir/h. Leak rate = Rate_pump - Net_rate = 1/5 - 1/6 = 6/30 - 5/30 = 1/30 reservoir/h. Time to empty full reservoir = 1 / (1/30) = 30 hours. Option C is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Pumprate = 1/5 pro Stunde. Nettorate mit Leck = 1/6 pro Stunde. Leckrate = 1/5 - 1/6 = 1/30 pro Stunde. Entleerungsdauer = 30 Stunden. Option C ist richtig.
questions.trap: Subtracting times directly: 6 - 5 = 1 hour, or multiplying 5 × 6 and doubting the result.
questions.trap_de: Zeiten direkt subtrahiert (6 - 5 = 1 h) statt Kehrwert-Differenz gebildet.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving: Work-Rate & Fluid Systems

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: A holding tank with a capacity of 4,200 liters is initially half-full of liquid. At 08:00, two inlet pipes (inflowing at 40 L/min and 60 L/min, respectively) and one drain pipe (outflowing at 30 L/min) are all opened simultaneously. At what time will the tank be completely full?
questions.question_de: Ein Auffangbecken mit 4.200 Litern Fassungsvermögen ist anfangs zur Hälfte gefüllt. Um 08:00 Uhr werden zwei Zulaufrohre (40 l/min bzw. 60 l/min) sowie ein Ablaufrohr (30 l/min) gleichzeitig geöffnet. Um wie viel Uhr ist das Becken randvoll?
questions.explanation: Initial volume = 4,200 / 2 = 2,100 liters. Volume needed to fill = 4,200 - 2,100 = 2,100 liters. Net inflow rate = 40 + 60 - 30 = 70 L/min. Time required = 2,100 L / (70 L/min) = 30 minutes. Completion time = 08:00 + 30 min = 08:30. Option D is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Anfangsvolumen = 2.100 l. Verbleibendes Füllvolumen = 2.100 l. Nettozufluss = 40 + 60 - 30 = 70 l/min. Zeitbedarf = 2.100 / 70 = 30 Minuten. Uhrzeit = 08:00 + 30 min = 08:30 Uhr. Option D ist richtig.
questions.trap: Calculating for the entire 4,200 liters without subtracting the initial half-full volume (yielding 60 min -> 09:00).
questions.trap_de: Vergessen, dass das Becken bereits halb voll war (4.200 / 70 = 60 min gerechnet).
questions.fast_track: Remaining volume = 2,100 L. Net rate = 70 L/min. Time = 2,100 / 70 = 30 min -> 08:30.
questions.fast_track_de: Restvolumen = 2.100 l. Nettozulauf = 70 l/min. Zeit = 30 min -> 08:30 Uhr.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving: Work-Rate & Fluid Systems

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: A technician needs to prepare 60 liters of a 30% saline solution by mixing a 20% saline solution with a 50% saline solution. How many liters of the 20% saline solution must be used?
questions.question_de: Ein Labortechniker möchte 60 Liter einer 30%igen Kochsalzlösung herstellen, indem er eine 20%ige und eine 50%ige Lösung mischt. Wie viele Liter der 20%igen Lösung müssen verwendet werden?
questions.explanation: Pearson's Square (diagonal difference): For 20% solution: |50 - 30| = 20 parts. For 50% solution: |20 - 30| = 10 parts. Ratio of 20% to 50% is 20 : 10 = 2 : 1. Total parts = 2 + 1 = 3. Amount of 20% solution = 60 × (2/3) = 40 liters. Option A is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Mischungskreuz: Anteil der 20%igen Lösung = |50 - 30| = 20 Teile. Anteil der 50%igen Lösung = |20 - 30| = 10 Teile. Verhältnis = 2 : 1. Summe = 3 Teile. Menge 20% = 60  (2/3) = 40 Liter. Option A ist richtig.
questions.trap: Equal mixing: 30 liters of each (would yield 35%), or inverting the ratio parts (giving 20 liters).
questions.trap_de: Gleiche Anteile angenommen (30 l) oder das Mischungsverhältnis vertauscht (20 l).
questions.fast_track_de: Mischungskreuz: 20 Teile zu 10 Teile = 2 : 1. 2/3 von 60 l = 40 Liter.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving: Mixtures & Dilution Concentrations

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: A chemistry lab has 40 liters of an 80% ethanol solution. How many liters of pure distilled water (0% ethanol) must be added to dilute the mixture to a 50% ethanol solution?
questions.question_de: Ein Chemielabor verfügt über 40 Liter einer 80%igen Ethanollösung. Wie viele Liter destilliertes Wasser (0% Ethanol) müssen hinzugefügt werden, um die Lösung auf eine Konzentration von 50% zu verdünnen?
questions.explanation: Solute mass conservation: Volume of pure ethanol = 40 L × 0.80 = 32 L. Let total final volume be V. Then 32 / V = 0.50 -> V = 32 / 0.50 = 64 L. Water added = V_final - V_initial = 64 - 40 = 24 liters. Option B is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Erhaltung der Reinstoffmenge: Reines Ethanol = 40 l  0,80 = 32 Liter. Neues Gesamtvolumen V: 32 / V = 0,50 -> V = 64 Liter. Zugefügtes Wasser = 64 - 40 = 24 Liter. Option B ist richtig.
questions.trap: Calculating 80% - 50% = 30% of 40 L = 12 L, or adding 32 L (thinking 32 L water balances 32 L ethanol to make 50% of 64, but adding from 40 L).
questions.trap_de: Differenz 30% von 40 l = 12 l gebildet, statt das neue Gesamtvolumen zu ermitteln.
questions.fast_track: Constant solute: 40 × 80 = V × 50 -> V = 64 L. Added water = 64 - 40 = 24 L.
questions.fast_track_de: 40  80 = V  50 -> V = 64 l. Zugefügt: 64 - 40 = 24 Liter.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving: Mixtures & Dilution Concentrations

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: A beaker contains 30 liters of a 10% hydrochloric acid solution. How many liters of pure concentrated hydrochloric acid (100%) must be added to raise the concentration of the solution to 25%?
questions.question_de: Ein Behälter enthält 30 Liter einer 10%igen Salzsäurelösung. Wie viele Liter reine konzentrierte Salzsäure (100%) müssen hinzugefügt werden, um den Säuregehalt auf 25% zu steigern?
questions.explanation: Pearson's square between 10% solution and 100% pure acid to achieve 25%: For 10% solution: |100 - 25| = 75 parts. For 100% acid: |10 - 25| = 15 parts. Ratio of 10% solution to 100% acid = 75 : 15 = 5 : 1. The 10% solution represents 5 parts = 30 L -> 1 part = 30 / 5 = 6.0 liters of pure acid. Option C is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Mischungskreuz: 10% Lösung hat |100 - 25| = 75 Teile; 100% Säure hat |25 - 10| = 15 Teile. Verhältnis = 75 : 15 = 5 : 1. 5 Teile entsprechen 30 l -> 1 Teil (reine Säure) = 30 / 5 = 6,0 Liter. Option C ist richtig.
questions.trap: Taking (25% - 10%) × 30 L = 15% × 30 = 4.5 L (ignoring that added acid increases the total solution volume).
questions.trap_de: 15% Zunahme auf das Ausgangsvolumen bezogen (15% von 30 l = 4,5 l), ohne das steigende Gesamtvolumen zu beachten.
questions.fast_track_de: Verhältnis = 75 : 15 = 5 : 1. Reinsäure = 30 / 5 = 6,0 Liter.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving: Mixtures & Dilution Concentrations

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: A jeweler melts together 300 grams of an 18-karat gold alloy (75% pure gold by mass) and 200 grams of a 12-karat gold alloy (50% pure gold by mass). What is the percentage of pure gold in the resulting 500-gram ingot?
questions.question_de: Ein Goldschmied schmilzt 300 Gramm einer 18-Karat-Goldlegierung (75% Feingehalt) und 200 Gramm einer 12-Karat-Goldlegierung (50% Feingehalt) zusammen. Welchen prozentualen Feingoldanteil besitzt der resultierende 500-Gramm-Barren?
questions.explanation: Mass of gold in first alloy = 300 g × 0.75 = 225 g. Mass of gold in second alloy = 200 g × 0.50 = 100 g. Total mass of gold = 225 + 100 = 325 g. Total mass of ingot = 300 + 200 = 500 g. Percentage = 325 / 500 = 650 / 1,000 = 65.0%. Option D is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Goldanteil Legierung 1 = 300 g  0,75 = 225 g. Goldanteil Legierung 2 = 200 g  0,50 = 100 g. Gesamtgold = 325 g bei 500 g Gesamtmasse. Feingehalt = 325 / 500 = 65,0%. Option D ist richtig.
questions.trap: Unweighted arithmetic average of percentages: (75% + 50%) / 2 = 62.5% (Option B), ignoring that the 18-karat alloy has greater mass.
questions.trap_de: Einfacher Durchschnitt der Prozentwerte: (75 + 50)/2 = 62,5% (Option B), ohne die Massen 300 g und 200 g zu gewichten.
questions.fast_track_de: Gewichteter Mittelwert: (3  75 + 2  50) / 5 = 325 / 5 = 65,0%.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving: Mixtures & Dilution Concentrations

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: A 50-liter container is completely filled with pure coolant concentrate (100%). Exactly 10 liters are removed and replaced with 10 liters of pure water, and the solution is mixed thoroughly. Then, 10 liters of this new mixture are removed and replaced again with 10 liters of pure water. What is the concentration of coolant concentrate in the container after the second replacement?
questions.question_de: Ein 50-Liter-Behälter ist randvoll mit reinem Kühlmittelkonzentrat (100%) gefüllt. Genau 10 Liter werden entnommen und durch 10 Liter reines Wasser ersetzt und gründlich vermischt. Anschließend werden erneut 10 Liter der Mischung entnommen und durch 10 Liter reines Wasser ersetzt. Welche Konzentration an Kühlmittel verbleibt im Behälter?
questions.explanation: Each replacement removes 10/50 = 1/5 of the current coolant, leaving 4/5 (80%) of the solute. After the 1st replacement: 100% × (4/5) = 80%. After the 2nd replacement: 80% × (4/5) = 64%. Or formula: (40/50)^2 = (4/5)^2 = 16/25 = 64%. Option A is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Jeder Schritt entfernt 10/50 = 1/5 des vorhandenen Kühlmittels, sodass 4/5 (80%) verbleiben. Nach 2 Schritten: (4/5)^2 = 16/25 = 64%. Option A ist richtig.
questions.trap: Subtracting 20% twice additively: 100% - 20% - 20% = 60%, or thinking it remains at 80% - 10% = 70%.
questions.trap_de: Lineare Subtraktion: 100% - 20% - 20% = 60%, statt multiplikativem Schwund (4/5  4/5).
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving: Work-Rate & Fluid Systems

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: A pharmaceutical batch is prepared by combining 20 liters of a 5% glucose solution and 30 liters of a 15% glucose solution. How many liters of a 25% glucose solution must be added to this combined mixture so that the final solution has an overall concentration of exactly 18%?
questions.question_de: Für eine Infusionslösung werden zunächst 20 Liter einer 5%igen Glukoselösung und 30 Liter einer 15%igen Glukoselösung gemischt. Wie viele Liter einer 25%igen Glukoselösung müssen hinzugefügt werden, damit die Gesamtlösung genau 18% Glukose enthält?
questions.explanation: Initial mixture volume = 20 + 30 = 50 L. Total glucose = 20 × 0.05 + 30 × 0.15 = 1.0 + 4.5 = 5.5 L. Concentration of initial mixture = 5.5 / 50 = 11%. Now mix 50 L of 11% solution with X liters of 25% solution to achieve 18%: Pearson's square gives |25 - 18| = 7 parts of 11% solution, and |18 - 11| = 7 parts of 25% solution. The ratio is 7 : 7 = 1 : 1. Therefore, X must equal exactly 50 liters. Option B is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Erste Mischung: 20 + 30 = 50 Liter mit 1,0 + 4,5 = 5,5 Liter Glukose (11%). Mischung von 50 l (11%) mit X Litern (25%) auf 18%: Mischungskreuz ergibt |25 - 18| : |18 - 11| = 7 : 7 = 1 : 1. Also muss genau gleich viel 25%ige Lösung zugegeben werden: X = 50 Liter. Option B ist richtig.
questions.trap: Averaging the three percentages directly: (5 + 15 + 25)/3 = 15%, or arithmetic slips in initial solute.
questions.trap_de: Unüberlegtes Mitteln der Prozentwerte oder Rechenfehler bei den Glukosemengen.
questions.fast_track_de: Ausgangskonzentration: 11%. Mischungsverhältnis zu 25% auf 18% ist 7:7 = 1:1 -> 50 Liter.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving: Mixtures & Dilution Concentrations

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: An industrial boiler contains 120 kg of a saline solution with a salt concentration of 5% by mass. Water is evaporated by heating until the salt concentration increases to 8% by mass. How many kilograms of water evaporated during this process?
questions.question_de: Ein Industriekessel enthält 120 kg einer Salzlösung mit einem Salzgehalt von 5 Massenprozent. Durch Erhitzen verdampft Wasser, bis der Salzgehalt auf 8 Massenprozent ansteigt. Wie viele Kilogramm Wasser sind dabei verdampft?
questions.explanation: Salt mass remains invariant: m_salt = 120 kg × 0.05 = 6 kg. In the final solution, these 6 kg represent 8% of the total mass M_final: 6 / M_final = 0.08 -> M_final = 6 / 0.08 = 600 / 8 = 75 kg. Evaporated water = M_initial - M_final = 120 - 75 = 45 kg. Option C is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Salzmenge bleibt konstant: 120 kg  0,05 = 6 kg. Diese 6 kg entsprechen 8% der neuen Masse M: M = 6 / 0,08 = 75 kg. Verdampftes Wasser = 120 - 75 = 45 kg. Option C ist richtig.
questions.trap: Calculating 8% - 5% = 3% of 120 kg = 3.6 kg evaporated water.
questions.trap_de: Prozentdifferenz (8% - 5% = 3%) auf 120 kg angewendet (3,6 kg) statt Massekonstanz des Salzes zu nutzen.
questions.fast_track: M_final = 6 / 0.08 = 75 kg. Evaporated = 120 - 75 = 45 kg.
questions.fast_track_de: M_neu = 6 / 0,08 = 75 kg -> 120 - 75 = 45 kg Wasser verdampft.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving: Mixtures & Dilution Concentrations

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: A specialty roaster blends two types of coffee beans: Grade A at €12 per kg and Grade B at €20 per kg. How many kilograms of Grade A must be blended to produce 40 kg of a blend that costs exactly €15 per kg?
questions.question_de: Eine Rösterei mischt zwei Kaffeesorten: Sorte A zu 12 €/kg und Sorte B zu 20 €/kg. Wie viele Kilogramm von Sorte A werden benötigt, um 40 kg einer Mischung mit einem Kilopreis von genau 15 € herzustellen?
questions.explanation: Pearson's Square applied to prices: For Grade A (€12): |20 - 15| = 5 parts. For Grade B (€20): |12 - 15| = 3 parts. Ratio of Grade A to Grade B = 5 : 3. Total parts = 5 + 3 = 8 parts. Each part = 40 kg / 8 = 5 kg. Mass of Grade A = 5 parts × 5 kg = 25 kg. Option D is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Mischungskreuz: Sorte A (12 €) hat |20 - 15| = 5 Teile; Sorte B (20 €) hat |12 - 15| = 3 Teile. Verhältnis A : B = 5 : 3. Gesamt: 8 Teile für 40 kg -> 1 Teil = 5 kg. Sorte A = 5  5 kg = 25 kg. Option D ist richtig.
questions.trap: Computing Grade B instead of Grade A (giving 15 kg, Option A), or choosing 20 kg (simple midpoint).
questions.trap_de: Menge von Sorte B berechnet (15 kg, Option A) statt Sorte A.
questions.fast_track: Pearson: 5 parts A : 3 parts B. Grade A = (5/8) × 40 = 25 kg.
questions.fast_track_de: Mischungskreuz: 5 Teile A zu 3 Teile B -> Sorte A = 5/8 von 40 = 25 kg.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving: Proportions & Financial Logic

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: A technician drives 60 km from the headquarters to a remote site at an average speed of 60 km/h, and returns along the exact same route in heavy evening traffic at an average speed of 40 km/h. What was the technician's average speed for the entire 120 km round trip?
questions.question_de: Ein Servicetechniker fährt eine Strecke von 60 km zu einem Kunden mit durchschnittlich 60 km/h und kehrt auf derselben Route bei dichtem Verkehr mit 40 km/h zurück. Wie hoch war die Durchschnittsgeschwindigkeit für die gesamten 120 km der Hin- und Rückfahrt?
questions.explanation: Average speed = Total distance / Total time. Outward time = 60 km / 60 km/h = 1.0 h. Return time = 60 km / 40 km/h = 1.5 h. Total time = 1.0 + 1.5 = 2.5 h. v_avg = 120 km / 2.5 h = 48 km/h. Alternatively, harmonic mean: 2v1v2 / (v1 + v2) = 26040 / 100 = 48 km/h. Option A is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Durchschnittsgeschwindigkeit = Gesamtstrecke / Gesamtzeit. Hinweg: 60/60 = 1 h. Rückweg: 60/40 = 1,5 h. Gesamtzeit: 2,5 h. v = 120 / 2,5 = 48 km/h. Harmonisches Mittel: 26040 / 100 = 48 km/h. Option A ist richtig.
questions.trap: Taking the arithmetic mean of the speeds: (60 + 40)/2 = 50 km/h (Option B) - the classic false average trap.
questions.trap_de: Arithmetisches Mittel gebildet: (60 + 40) / 2 = 50 km/h (Option B), statt über Zeiten zu mitteln.
questions.fast_track_de: Harmonisches Mittel: 2  60  40 / 100 = 48 km/h.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Mathematics & Physics: Kinematic Rates & Speed

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: Two railway stations, X and Y, are 310 km apart on a straight track. Train 1 departs Station X at 09:00 traveling towards Y at a constant speed of 80 km/h. Train 2 departs Station Y at 09:30 traveling towards X at a constant speed of 100 km/h. At what time do the two trains pass each other?
questions.question_de: Zwei Bahnhöfe X und Y sind 310 km voneinander entfernt. Zug 1 fährt um 09:00 Uhr in X mit konstanten 80 km/h in Richtung Y ab. Zug 2 fährt um 09:30 Uhr in Y mit konstanten 100 km/h in Richtung X ab. Um wie viel Uhr begegnen sich die beiden Züge?
questions.explanation: From 09:00 to 09:30 (0.5 hours), Train 1 travels alone: d = 80 km/h × 0.5 h = 40 km. Remaining distance between the trains at 09:30 = 310 - 40 = 270 km. Relative speed towards each other = 80 + 100 = 180 km/h. Time to meet after 09:30 = 270 km / 180 km/h = 1.5 hours (1 hour 30 min). Meeting time = 09:30 + 1:30 = 11:00. Option B is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Zwischen 09:00 und 09:30 Uhr legt Zug 1 bereits 40 km zurück. Restdistanz um 09:30 Uhr = 310 - 40 = 270 km. Relativgeschwindigkeit = 80 + 100 = 180 km/h. Zeit bis zur Begegnung = 270 / 180 = 1,5 Stunden (90 min). Uhrzeit = 09:30 + 1:30 = 11:00 Uhr. Option B ist richtig.
questions.trap: Ignoring Train 1's 30-minute head start and computing 310 / 180 ≈ 1.72 h from 09:00.
questions.trap_de: Den Vorsprung von 30 Minuten ignoriert und 310 / 180 gerechnet.
questions.fast_track_de: Reststrecke: 270 km. Zeit: 270 / 180 = 1,5 h ab 09:30 -> 11:00 Uhr.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Mathematics & Physics: Kinematic Rates & Speed

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: A high-speed passenger train of length 150 meters travels at 72 km/h on a parallel track. It catches up to and overtakes a freight train of length 250 meters traveling in the same direction at 36 km/h. How many seconds elapse from the moment the front of the passenger train reaches the rear of the freight train until the rear of the passenger train completely clears the front of the freight train?
questions.question_de: Ein 150 m langer Personenzug fährt mit 72 km/h auf einem Parallelgleis. Er holt einen 250 m langen Güterzug ein, der in dieselbe Richtung mit 36 km/h fährt. Wie viele Sekunden vergehen von dem Moment, in dem die Spitze des Personenzugs das Ende des Güterzugs erreicht, bis sein Heck die Spitze des Güterzugs komplett passiert hat?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 72 km/h - 36 km/h = 36 km/h. Converting to m/s: 36 / 3.6 = 10 m/s. Total distance that must be covered relative to the freight train = Length_passenger + Length_freight = 150 m + 250 m = 400 m. Time = 400 m / (10 m/s) = 40 seconds. Option C is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Relativgeschwindigkeit = 72 - 36 = 36 km/h = 10 m/s. Relativ zurückzulegende Strecke = Summe beider Zuglängen = 150 + 250 = 400 m. Dauer = 400 m / 10 m/s = 40 Sekunden. Option C ist richtig.
questions.trap: Using only one of the train lengths: 250 / 10 = 25 s (Option A) or 150 / 10 = 15 s.
questions.trap_de: Nur eine der beiden Zuglängen berücksichtigt (250 / 10 = 25 s) statt der Summe.
questions.fast_track_de: v_rel = 10 m/s. Strecke = 400 m -> t = 400 / 10 = 40 s.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Mathematics & Physics: Kinematic Rates & Speed

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: A survey motorboat travels a 48 km stretch downstream with the river current in 2 hours. Returning upstream against the current along the exact same stretch takes 3 hours. Assuming constant engine throttle and constant water flow, what is the speed of the river current?
questions.question_de: Ein Messboot legt eine 48 km lange Flussstrecke flussabwärts (mit der Strömung) in 2 Stunden zurück. Flussaufwärts (gegen die Strömung) benötigt dasselbe Boot für die 48 km genau 3 Stunden. Wie hoch ist die Fließgeschwindigkeit des Flusses?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed: v_down = v_boat + v_current = 48 km / 2 h = 24 km/h. Upstream speed: v_up = v_boat - v_current = 48 km / 3 h = 16 km/h. Subtracting the two equations: 2v_current = 24 - 16 = 8 km/h -> v_current = 4.0 km/h. Option D is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Geschwindigkeit stromabwärts: v_Boot + v_Fluss = 48 / 2 = 24 km/h. Stromaufwärts: v_Boot - v_Fluss = 48 / 3 = 16 km/h. Differenz = 2v_Fluss = 24 - 16 = 8 km/h -> v_Fluss = 4,0 km/h. Option D ist richtig.
questions.trap: Subtracting downstream and upstream speeds directly (24 - 16 = 8 km/h) without dividing by 2.
questions.trap_de: Vergessen, die Geschwindigkeitsdifferenz durch 2 zu teilen (8 km/h statt 4 km/h).
questions.fast_track: v_current = (v_down - v_up) / 2 = (24 - 16) / 2 = 4.0 km/h.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Problem Solving: Work-Rate & Fluid Systems

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: Two cyclists start simultaneously from the exact same starting line on a 1,200-meter circular track, riding in opposite directions. Cyclist A maintains a constant speed of 12 m/s, and Cyclist B maintains a constant speed of 8 m/s. How many seconds after the start will they cross paths for the third time?
questions.question_de: Zwei Radfahrer starten gleichzeitig an derselben Startlinie einer 1.200 m langen Rundbahn in entgegengesetzte Richtungen. Radfahrer A fährt konstant mit 12 m/s, Radfahrer B mit 8 m/s. Nach wie vielen Sekunden begegnen sie sich zum dritten Mal?
questions.explanation: Because they travel in opposite directions, their relative speed of approach is v_rel = 12 + 8 = 20 m/s. Each encounter requires them to collectively cover one full lap of 1,200 meters. Time for 1 encounter = 1,200 m / 20 m/s = 60 seconds. For the 3rd encounter, time = 3 × 60 s = 180 seconds. Option A is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Entgegengesetzte Fahrtrichtung -> Relativgeschwindigkeit = 12 + 8 = 20 m/s. Eine gemeinsame Runde = 1.200 m. Zeit pro Begegnung = 1.200 / 20 = 60 Sekunden. Dritte Begegnung = 3  60 = 180 Sekunden. Option A ist richtig.
questions.trap: Calculating only for the 1st encounter (60 s), or using speed difference 12 - 8 = 4 m/s (as if traveling in the same direction).
questions.trap_de: Differenz statt Summe gebildet (12 - 8 = 4 m/s) oder nur die erste Begegnung berechnet.
questions.fast_track: v_rel = 20 m/s. 1 lap = 60 s. 3rd meeting = 3 × 60 = 180 s.
questions.fast_track_de: Relativtempo = 20 m/s. 1.200 / 20 = 60 s pro Treffen -> 3. Treffen = 180 s.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Mathematics & Physics: Kinematic Rates & Speed

questions.subject: Core Mathematics
questions.question: A delivery truck leaves a distribution center traveling along a highway at a steady speed of 75 km/h. Exactly 40 minutes later, an express dispatch car departs from the same center following the same route at a steady speed of 105 km/h. At what distance from the distribution center does the dispatch car catch up with the truck?
questions.question_de: Ein Lieferwagen verlässt ein Logistikzentrum mit konstanten 75 km/h auf der Autobahn. Genau 40 Minuten später fährt ein Eilkurier am selben Zentrum los und folgt derselben Route mit 105 km/h. In welcher Entfernung vom Logistikzentrum holt der Eilkurier den Lieferwagen ein?
questions.explanation: Truck head start time = 40 min = 40/60 h = 2/3 h. Lead distance = 75 km/h × (2/3) h = 50 km. Relative speed = 105 - 75 = 30 km/h. Time to catch up = 50 km / 30 km/h = 5/3 hours (100 minutes). Distance from center = Speed_car × Time = 105 km/h × (5/3) h = 35 × 5 = 175 km. Option B is correct.
questions.explanation_de: Vorsprung des Lkw = 40 min = 2/3 h  75 km/h = 50 km. Relativgeschwindigkeit = 105 - 75 = 30 km/h. Aufholzeit = 50 / 30 = 5/3 Stunden. Treffpunkt-Distanz = 105 km/h  5/3 h = 175 km. Option B ist richtig.
questions.trap: Multiplying 105 by 40 directly without time conversion, or thinking 50 km lead is the overtake distance.
questions.trap_de: 40 Minuten nicht in Stunden umgerechnet oder 50 km Vorsprung fälschlicherweise als Antwort gewählt.
questions.fast_track: Lead = 50 km. Overtake time = 50/30 = 5/3 h. Distance = 105 × 5/3 = 175 km.
questions.fast_track_de: Vorsprung: 50 km. Aufholzeit: 5/3 h -> Strecke: 105  (5/3) = 175 km.
questions.imatBadge: 🏷️ IMAT Overlap: Mathematics & Physics: Kinematic Rates & Speed

questions.explanation: Relationship: Hand tool to its designated mechanical fastener. A hammer is designed specifically to drive a nail into a substrate; a screwdriver is designed specifically to drive a threaded screw. Both pairs express the identical Functional Tool : Fastener relationship.
questions.explanation_de: Beziehung: Handwerkzeug zu dem dafür vorgesehenen mechanischen Verbindungselement (Befestigungsmittel). Ein Hammer treibt einen Nagel ein; ein Schraubendreher dreht eine Schraube ein. Beide Paare repräsentieren dieselbe funktionale Werkzeug-Befestigungsmittel-Zuordnung.
questions.fast_track: Identify the category: Tool : Driven fastener -> Hammer drives nail; screwdriver drives screw.
questions.fast_track_de: Kategorie erkennen: Werkzeug : Verbindungselement -> Hammer treibt Nagel; Schraubendreher treibt Schraube.
questions.question:
Identify the word pair that completes the analogy in the same way:

Hammer : ________ = Screwdriver : ________
questions.question_de:
Bestimmen Sie das Wortpaar, das die Analogie in derselben Weise vervollständigt:

Hammer : ________ = Schraubendreher : ________
questions.subject: Core Logic & Reasoning
questions.trap: Selecting Wood : Sheet metal, which represents workpiece materials rather than the fasteners driven by the tools.
questions.trap_de: Holz : Blech gewählt (dies sind bearbeitete Werkstoffe, nicht die Verbindungselemente selbst).

questions.explanation: Relationship: Machine tool to its primary cutting/machining process (DIN 8589 cutting technologies). A lathe performs rotational turning (workpiece rotates, tool feeds linearly); a milling machine performs milling operations using a rotating multi-edged cutter against a feeding workpiece.
questions.explanation_de: Beziehung: Werkzeugmaschine zu ihrem primären spanenden Fertigungsverfahren nach DIN 8589. Auf einer Drehmaschine erfolgt das Drehen (rotierendes Werkstück); auf einer Fräsmaschine erfolgt das Fräsen mit rotierendem Mehrschneidenwerkzeug.
questions.fast_track: Machine tool to standard machining kinematic: Lathe -> Turning; Milling machine -> Milling.
questions.fast_track_de: Werkzeugmaschine zum Fertigungsverfahren: Drehmaschine -> Drehen; Fräsmaschine -> Fräsen.
questions.question:
Complete the manufacturing technology analogy:

Lathe : Turning = Milling Machine : ________

Ergänzen Sie die fertigungstechnische Analogie:

Drehmaschine : Drehen = Fräsmaschine : ________

questions.trap: Selecting grinding, which belongs to abrasive machining tools (grinding machines), not milling machines.
questions.trap_de: Schleifen gewählt (gehört zu Schleifmaschinen mit gebundenem Schleifmittel, nicht zur Fräsmaschine).

questions.explanation: Relationship: Tool (applicator) to its specialized consumable fastener. A blind rivet gun (riveter) sets a blind rivet into joined sheets; a staple gun drives a staple. Option C matches perfectly.
questions.explanation_de: Beziehung: Fügewerkzeug zum spezifischen Verbindungselement. Eine Blindnietzange verarbeitet Blindniete; ein Handtacker (Heftgerät) treibt Heftklammern ein. Option C ist präzise.
questions.fast_track: Fastener applicator : Fastener -> Rivet gun : Rivet = Staple gun : Staple.
questions.fast_track_de: Fügewerkzeug : Verbindungselement -> Blindnietzange : Niet = Tacker : Klammer.

questions.explanation: Relationship: Cutting tool to the geometric cavity or feature it cuts into a solid workpiece. A twist drill cuts a cylindrical bore (hole); a tap (Gewindebohrer) cuts an internal helical thread inside a pre-drilled bore. (A die / Schneideisen cuts an external thread).
questions.explanation_de: Beziehung: Zerspanungswerkzeug zum erzeugten Formelement. Ein Spiralbohrer erzeugt eine zylindrische Bohrung; ein Gewindebohrer schneidet ein Innengewinde in das Kernloch (während ein Schneideisen ein Außengewinde fertigt).
questions.fast_track: Tool to cavity profile: Drill -> Bore; Tap -> Internal thread.
questions.fast_track_de: Werkzeug zur Kontur: Bohrer -> Kernbohrung; Gewindebohrer -> Innengewinde.

Complete the machining operation analogy:

Twist drill : Cylindrical bore = Screw tap : ________

Spiralbohrer : Zylindrische Bohrung = Gewindebohrer : ________

questions.trap_de: Außengewinde gewählt (wird durch ein Schneideisen gefertigt, nicht durch einen Gewindebohrer).

questions.explanation: Relationship: Thermal joining device to its consumed solid filler/bonding material that is melted during the joining process. A soldering iron melts solder (Lötzinn); a hot-melt glue gun melts a thermoplastic adhesive stick.
questions.explanation_de: Beziehung: Thermisches Fügewerkzeug zu dem dabei aufgeschmolzenen festen Zusatz- bzw. Klebstoff. Ein Lötkolben schmilzt Lötdraht/Lötzinn; eine Heißklebepistole schmilzt thermoplastische Schmelzklebestifte.
questions.fast_track: Thermal applicator : Melted joining consumable -> Soldering iron melts solder; glue gun melts adhesive stick.
questions.fast_track_de: Thermischer Applikator : Schmelzendes Zusatzmaterial -> Lötkolben schmilzt Zinn; Klebepistole schmilzt Klebestift.

questions.trap_de: Flussmittel gewählt (Hilfsstoff zur Oxidentfernung, nicht das aufgeschmolzene Fügematerial selbst).

questions.explanation: Relationship: Forming/cutting equipment to its standard DIN production operation. Shears execute linear separation (shear cutting / Scherschneiden); a punch press executes piercing/punching (Lochen / Durchstanzen) via a closed-contour punch and die.
questions.explanation_de: Beziehung: Blechbearbeitungswerkzeug zum DIN-Fertigungsverfahren. Die Blechschere trennt entlang offener Schnittlinien (Scherschneiden); die Lochstanze trennt geschlossene Innenformen durch Lochen/Durchstanzen.
questions.fast_track: Tool : Separation kinematic -> Shears : Shear cutting = Punch : Piercing/Punching.
questions.fast_track_de: Trennwerkzeug : Wirkungsweise -> Schere : Scherschneiden = Stanze : Lochen.
